title: Extending finite-model derivations to the generic formal fibre
statement: Let A be a Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] that is integrally closed in its fraction field K [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let q be a prime ideal, and let C be the maximal-ideal-adic completion of A_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let M/K be finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and let B be an A-subalgebra of M finite as an A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with fraction field M. Put R=M tensor_K (K tensor_A C) [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Every absolute derivation D:B -> B (additive and satisfying D(bc)=bD(c)+cD(b)) extends to an absolute derivation E:R -> R such that E(b tensor 1)=D(b) tensor 1 for every b in B. The map A -> M is the composite A -> K -> M; R is allowed to be the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 07PR, finite-model and derivation extension paragraphs; Tag 07PE(1),(2); Algebra Tag 07N9

proof.text: Use normality and purelyInseparable_integral_prime_unique to obtain the unique prime r of B above q. Its prime fiber is a Unique type.

Apply completion_finite_extension to A and B. Collapse its product over the unique prime using RingEquiv.piUnique. Compose tensor commutation and cancelBaseChange to obtain the M-algebra equivalence R = M tensor_K (K tensor_A completion(A_q)) with M tensor_B completion(B_r).

Extend D to B_r by IsLocalization.extendDerivation (the proved square-zero localization construction), then to its completion by exists_completion_and_unique_localization. IsLocalization.tensorRight identifies M tensor_B completion(B_r) as the localization of completion(B_r) at the nonzero elements of B. Extend once more by the quotient rule.

Conjugate the last derivation by the ring equivalence. Its agreement on B follows successively from the three extension identities. The equivalence is M-linear, and the tensor balancing identity moves b from the M factor to the completed factor. No nontriviality of the final ring is used.

theorem exists_formalFiber_extension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed A] (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (M : Type v) [Field M] [Algebra (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField M]
    [Algebra A M] [IsScalarTower A (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField M]
    [Module.Finite (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField M]
    [IsPurelyInseparable (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField M]
    (B : Subalgebra A M) [Module.Finite A B] [IsFractionRing B M]
    (D : Derivation ℤ B B) :
    let C := AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
      (Localization.AtPrime q)
    let R := TensorProduct (⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField M ((⊥ : Ideal A).Fiber C)
    ∃ E : Derivation ℤ R R, ∀ b : B,
      E (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (b : M)) =
        Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (D b : M)
